answer: Sybil farms collapse once each identity must prove a distinct physical machine. Every applicant signs a timing trace of its kernel scheduler, and a verifier called JitterJudge compares that nanosecond noise against every trace already stored, refusing twins. The penalty trigger is a replay burn that seizes the bond and ejects both addresses once two identities share one fingerprint. A fake costs one rented core at four cents an hour, a thirty POA bond and twelve minutes of setup, so N fakes cost N times that plus the copper and opal for spare boards, and bulk registration stops paying.
